title: Lucky two-digit codes
observableEvidence: Counts ordered two-digit codes by parity cases while enforcing the no-repeated-digit condition.
prompt: A two-digit code uses two different digits chosen from 1, 2, 3, and 4. A code is called lucky if the sum of its digits is even. How many lucky codes are possible?

contestFormat.eligibility: Grade 8 or below and age 15.5 years or younger on the official contest date.

answerChoices.label: A
answerChoices.rationale: Counts only the unordered same-parity pairs {1,3} and {2,4}, not the two possible orders for each pair.

answerChoices.label: B
answerChoices.rationale: Correct: the ordered lucky codes are 13, 31, 24, and 42.

answerChoices.label: C
answerChoices.rationale: Chooses any 2 of the 4 digits, which counts unordered pairs and ignores the even-sum condition.

answerChoices.label: D
answerChoices.rationale: Allows repeated same-parity codes as well as different-digit codes: 2×2 odd choices plus 2×2 even choices.

answerChoices.label: E
answerChoices.rationale: Counts all different-digit two-digit codes, 4 choices for the tens digit and 3 for the ones digit, without applying the even-sum condition.

solutionRepresentation: An even digit sum happens when both digits have the same parity. The odd digits 1 and 3 make 13 and 31. The even digits 2 and 4 make 24 and 42. That gives 4 lucky codes.
solutionMethod: Split into odd-odd and even-even cases, then count ordered codes with no repeated digits.

deterministicValidator.equivalenceNotes: Accept the count with or without units or as choice B.

hintSteps.prompt: Focus on the parity of the two digits rather than listing every code immediately.
hintSteps.question: When is the sum of two digits even?

hintSteps.prompt: Make one case for two odd digits and another case for two even digits, remembering that the order of a two-digit code matters.
hintSteps.question: How can you list each case without repeating a digit?

hintSteps.prompt: For a code using A and B, AB and BA are different because the tens and ones places are different.
hintSteps.question: Which answer choice matches your ordered same-parity list?

review.originalityStatement: Original AMC 8-style draft written for this repository from the approved dossier's topic family and format constraints; no AMC 8 or AJHSME problem, wording, answer-choice set, diagram, or solution is reproduced.

accessibilityNotes: The digit set and code rule are fully textual; a learner can use a two-column parity list instead of a diagram.
accessibleAlternative: Read aloud or display: Choose two different digits from 1, 2, 3, and 4 to make an ordered two-digit code. Count the codes whose digit sum is even.
